hazards.source_text: In the episode of 1957 the maximum was placed towards the northwest of the capital, causing a flood that flooded the city of Valencia due to the overflow of the river Turia.

hazards.source_text: During the 1982 event, the peak focused on the central-southwestern area of the province, resulting in the well-known 'Tous Pantanada' due to the break-up of the dam that caused serious flooding downstream of the Júcar River.

hazards.source_text: In 1987, the highest rainfall focused on the Safor regions, on 3 November, and on the Ribera Alta region on 4 November.

hazards.source_text: Regarding the 2024 event, the low rainfall throughout the coast stands out, in contrast to the large accumulations of only tens of kilometres inland, focusing on the area of maximum precipitation in the interior of the province and north-western part of the south coastal warning zone.

hazards.source_text: The absolute precipitation peaks accumulated in twenty-four hours (official values) of each episode were 494,4 mm (1957), 635,2 mm (1982), 817.0 mm (1987) and 771,8 mm (2024).

hazards.source_text: However, it should be noted that the last episode has broken the national record of the intensity of the precipitation accumulated in one, six and twelve hours.

hazards.source_text: The maximum time data, of 185 mm, triples to the value of 60 mm used as threshold for the definition of torrentiality, being also 26 mm higher than the maximum value previously observed in the town of Vinaròs (Castellón) on 19 October 2018.

hazards.source_text: As for the accumulated values in six and twelve hours (621 and 720 mm, respectively) these double to the most extremes previously recorded in the station of Alpandeira (Málaga) on 21 October 2018.
